---
title: "Syncing metadata files with `.zenodo.toml`"
description: |
  Use the `sync` command to sync metadata from `.zenodo.toml` to other metadata files.
order: 2
---

The `.zenodo.toml` file contains metadata about a deposit on Zenodo. Other
metadata files can also describe deposits, such as `.zenodo.json`, or contain
similar metadata about a project alongside other information, such as
`CITATION.cff` or `pyproject.toml`.

zen-do can sync metadata from `.zenodo.toml` to other metadata files to help
keep everything consistent. Currently, zen-do supports syncing to `.zenodo.json`
and `CITATION.cff`, with plans to add support for `_quarto.yml`,
`pyproject.toml`, `codemeta.json`, and `DESCRIPTION` in the future.

zen-do expects the target metadata file to be in the same folder as
`.zenodo.toml`. If the target metadata file doesn't exist in that folder, it
will be created there and populated with metadata from `.zenodo.toml`. If it
already exists, its metadata will be updated.

During syncing, fields present in `.zenodo.toml` will be updated in the target
metadata file. Fields in the target file that are not present in `.zenodo.toml`
will be left unchanged.

For example, to sync `CITATION.cff` with `.zenodo.toml`, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do sync path/to/.zenodo.toml --to citation-cff
```

If you omit the path to `.zenodo.toml`, it will default to `.zenodo.toml` in the
working directory.
